basis.saw: Flowchart panel headed '3. Evaluation Pipeline'; lower part of Figure 1 (continues from img-p005-2).

narrative.text: Figure 1, part 3 'Evaluation Pipeline': a PDF-Parser produces Parsed Text (TXT); together with Ground Truth (JSON list of text, inline-formula and display-formula items) it feeds 'LLM-Based Matching (+ Rule-Based Post-Verification)', which outputs Formula Pairs (JSON of gt_formula/parsed_formula, e.g. $a+1$ vs $a+I$) and then 'Evaluation for all formula pairs'.

basis.saw: Flowchart panels '1. Formula Dataset' and '2. Benchmark Dataset'; upper part of Figure 1.

narrative.text: Figure 1, parts 1-2: Formula Dataset (Wikipedia → Formula Extraction → Filtering + Deduplication → wikipedia-latex-formulas-319k, with a Hugging Face emoji logo), then Benchmark Dataset: randomized building blocks (Display Formulas, Text Segments, Text + Inline Formulas Mixed) form a Ground Truth JSON, combined with a randomized Layout/Style LaTeX template into an assembled TEX file, compiled by pdflatex into the PDF to be parsed.

basis.saw: Two CDM symbol-matching comparisons with score tables (illustrating rater disagreement).

narrative.text: Two formula comparisons rendered by the CDM tool (green boxes = matched symbols, red = errors), each with a score table. Left: 778320/2598960 vs 778120/2598960 (one digit red): LLM-Judge 3, CDM 0.929, human scores 1, 3, 9. Right: (1 + r/n)^n vs (1 + r/a)^n (denominator red): LLM-Judge 2, CDM 0.875, human scores 1, 4, 7.

basis.saw: Four CDM comparison panels with all-green boxes; illustrates CDM false positives (text p.10).

narrative.text: Four ground-truth/parsed formula pairs separated by a blue line, all symbols boxed green: 7^2 vs 72, 10^{-1} vs 10 − 1, x_{(i−1)} vs x(i − 1), and blackboard ℕ ⊂ ℝ vs italic N ⊂ R. These are the examples of CDM giving matches despite positional or symbol differences.

basis.saw: Four CDM comparison panels with red-boxed operator symbols; illustrates CDM false negatives.

narrative.text: Four formula pairs that look equivalent but where CDM boxes the middle symbol in red: A ∧ B, A \ B = 0, x → y, and x ≠ y, each shown above and below a blue line with the operands boxed green.
